circumflexion: 1. The act of bending, or causing to assume a curved form. 2. A winding about; a turning; a circuity; a fold.
cisatlantic: On this side of the Atlantic Ocean; -- used of the eastern or the western side, according to the standpoint of the writer. Story.
cizar: To clip with scissors. (old) Beau. & Fl.
cicisbeism: The state or conduct of a cicisbeo.
circumambulate: To walk round about. -- Cir`cum*am`bu*la"tion, n.
cimbrian: Of or pertaining to the Cimbri. -- n. One of the Cimbri. See Cimbric.
cinch: 1. A strong saddle girth, as of canvas. [West. U. S.] 2. A tight grip. [Colloq.]
cirrhotic: Pertaining to, caused by, or affected with, cirrhosis; as, cirrhotic degeneration; a cirrhotic liver.
circumstantiable: Capable of being circumstantiated. (old) Jer Taylor.
circumscriptible: Capable of being circumscribed or limited by bounds.
cicala: A cicada. See Cicada. "At eve a dry cicala sung." Tennison.
circumvallate: To surround with a rampart or wall. Johnson. | 1. Surrounded with a wall; inclosed with a rampart. 2. (Anat.) Surrounded by a ridle or elevation; as, the circumvallate papillæ, near the base of the tongue.
circumfusile: Capable of being poured or spread round. "Circumfusile gold." Pope.
cicatrizant: A medicine or application that promotes the healing of a sore or wound, or the formation of a cicatrix.
ciborium: 1. (Arch.) A canopy usually standing free and supported on four columns, covering the high altar, or, very rarely, a secondary altar. 2. (R. C. Ch.) The coffer or case in which the host is kept; the pyx.
citrus: A genus of trees including the orange, lemon, citron, etc., originally natives of southern Asia.
circler: A mean or inferior poet, perhaps from his habit of wandering around as a stroller; an itinerant poet. Also, a name given to the cyclic poets. See under Cyclic, a. (old) B. Jonson.
circumdenudation: Denudation around or in the neighborhood of an object. Hills of circumdenudation, hills which have been produced by surface erosion; the elevations which have been left, after denudation of a mass of high ground. Jukes.
circularity: The quality or state of being circular; a circular form.
civility: 1. The state of society in which the relations and duties of a citizen are recognized and obeyed; a state of civilization. (old) Monarchies have risen from barbarrism to civility, and fallen again to ruin. Sir J. Davies. The gradual depature of all deeper signification from the word civility has obliged the creation of another word -- civilization. Trench. 2.
circuitous: Going round in a circuit; roundabout; indirect; as, a circuitous road; a circuitous manner of accompalishing an end. -- Cir*cu"i*tous*ly, adv. -- Cir*cu"i*tous*ness, n. Syn. -- Tortuous; winding; sinuous; serpentine.
cirriferous: Bearing cirri, as many plants and animals.
circulatory: 1. Circular; as, a circulatory letter. Johnson. 2. Circulating, or going round. T. Warton. 3. (Anat.) Subserving the purposes of circulation; as, circulatory organs; | A chemical vessel consisting of two portions unequally exposed to the heat of the fire, and with connecting pipes or passages, through which the fluid rises from the overheated portion, and descends…
cinquecentist: 1. An Italian of the sixteenth century, esp. a poet or artist. 2. A student or imitator of the art or literature of the Cinquecento.
circumscriptive: Circumscribing or tending to circumscribe; marcing the limits or form of.
circumventor: One who circumvents; one who gains his purpose by cunning.
cinquepace: A lively dance (called also galliard), the steps of which were regulated by the number five. (old) Nares. Shak.
cirrigrade: Moving or moved by cirri, or hairlike appendages.
cittern: An instrument shaped like a lute, but strung with wire and played with a quill or plectrum. [Written also cithern.] Shak. Note: Not to be confounded with zither.
civilized: Reclaimed from savage life and manners; instructed in arts, learning, and civil manners; refined; cultivated. Sale of conscience and duty in open market is not reconcilable with the present state of civilized society. J. Quincy.
cirrate: Having cirri along the margin of a part or organ.
cirripedia: An order of Crustacea including the barnacles. When adult, they have a calcareous shell composed of several pieces. From the opening of the shell the animal throws out a group of curved legs, looking like a delicate curl, whence the name of the group. See Anatifa.
circulary: Circular; illogical. [Obs. & .] "Cross and circulary speeches." Hooker.
cirrose: (a) Bearing a tendril or tendrils; as, a cirrose leaf. (b) Resembling a tendril or cirrus. [Spelt also cirrhose.]
cisleithan: On the Austrian side of the river Leitha; Austrian.
citied: 1. Belonging to, or resembling, a city. "Smoky, citied towns" Drayton. 2. Containing, or covered with, cities. "The citied earth." Keats.
ciderkin: A kind of weak cider made by steeping the refuse pomace in water. Ciderkin is made for common drinking, and supplies the place of small beer. Mortimer.
circumposition: The act of placing in a circle, or round about, or the state of being so placed. Evelyn.
cinnabarine: Pertaining to, or resembling, cinnabar; consisting of cinnabar, or containing it; as, cinnabarine sand.
cinchona: 1. (Bot.) A genus of trees growing naturally on the Andes in Peru and adjacent countries, but now cultivated in the East Indies, producing a medicinal bark of great value. 2. (Med.) The bark of any species of cinchona containing three per cent. or more of bitter febrifuge alkaloids; Peruvian bark; Jesuits' bark.
cicatricle: The germinating point in the embryo of a seed; the point in the yolk of an egg at which development begins.
circumfluent: Flowing round; surrounding in the manner of a fluid. "The deep, circumfluent waves." Pope.
cigarette: A little cigar; a little fine tobacco rolled in paper for smoking.
cithara: An ancient instrument resembling the harp.
circumfusion: The act of pouring or spreading round; the state of being spread round. Swift.
cicely: Any one of several umbelliferous plants, of the genera Myrrhis, Osmorrhiza, etc.
cinchonic: Belonging to, or obtained from, cinchona. Mayne.
circumjacent: Lying round; borderong on every side. T. Fuller.
circumscissile: Dehiscing or opening by a transverse fissure extending around (a capsule or pod). See Illust. of Pyxidium.
circumscription: 1. An inscription written around anything. Ashmole. 2. The exterior line which determines the form or magnitude of a body; outline; periphery. Ray. 3. The act of limiting, or the state of being limited, by conditions or restraints; bound; confinement; limit. The circumscriptions of terrestrial nature. Johnson.
circuit: 1. The act of moving or revolving around, or as in a circle or orbit; a revolution; as, the periodical circuit of the earth round the sun. Watts. 2. The circumference of, or distance round, any… | To move in a circle; to go round; to circulate. (old) J. Philips.
cirrhosis: A disease of the liver in which it usually becomes smaller in size and more dense and fibrous in consistence; hence sometimes applied to similar changes in other organs, caused by increase in the fibrous framework and decrease in the proper substance of the organ.
circumlocutional: Relating to, or consisting of, circumlocutions; periphrastic; circuitous.
ciceronian: Resembling Cicero in style or action; eloquent.
civilservicereform: The substitution of business principles and methods for political methods in the conduct of the civil service. esp. the merit system instead of the spoils system in making appointments to office.
ciliograde: Moving by means of cilia, or cilialike organs; as, the ciliograde Medusæ.
cinnoline: A nitrogenous organic base, C8H6N2, analogous to quinoline, obtained from certain complex diazo compounds.
circumambage: A roundabout or indirect course; indirectness. (old) S. Richardson.
cipolin: A whitish marble, from Rome, containiing pale greenish zones. It consists of calcium carbonate, with zones and cloudings of talc.
circumbendibus: A roundabout or indirect way. [Jocular] Goldsmith.
circuity: A going round in a circle; a course not direct; a roundabout way of proceeding.
cicutoxin: The active principle of the water hemlock (Cicuta) extracted as a poisonous gummy substance.
circumflex: 1. A wave of the voice embracing both a rise and fall or a fall and a rise on the same a syllable. Walker. 2. A character, or accent, denoting in Greek a rise and of the voice on the same long… | To mark or pronounce with a circumflex. Walker.
circum: A Latin preposition, used as a prefix in many English words, and signifying around or about.
cist: 1. (Antiq.) A box or chest. Specifically: (a) A bronze receptacle, round or oval, frequently decorated with engravings on the sides and cover, and with feet, handles, etc., of decorative castings. (b) A cinerary urn. See Illustration in Appendix. 2. See Cyst.
circulate: 1. To move in a circle or circuitously; to move round and return to the same point; as, the blood circulates in the body. Boyle. 2. To pass from place to place, from person to person, or from hand to… | To cause to pass from place to place, or from person to person; to spread; as, to circulate a report; to circulate bills of credit. Circulating pump. See under Pump. Syn. -- To spread; diffuse;
circinate: Rolled together downward, the tip occupying the center; -- a term used in reference to foliation or leafing, as in ferns. Gray. | To make a circle around; to encompass. (old) Bailey.
circulatorious: Travelling from house to house or from town to town; itinerant. (old) "Circulatorious jugglers." Barrow.
citrination: The process by which anything becomes of the color of a lemon; esp., in alchemy, the state of perfection in the philosopher's stone indicated by its assuming a deep yellow color. Thynne.
ciliated: Provided with, or surrounded by, cilia; as, a ciliate leaf; endowed with vibratory motion; as, the ciliated epithelium of the windpipe.
circumventive: Tending to circumvent; deceiving by artifices; deluding.
circumvent: To gain advantage over by arts, stratagem, or deception; to decieve; to delude; to get around. I circumvented whom I could not gain. Dryden.
cimbric: Pertaining to the Cimbri, an ancient tribe inhabiting Northern Germany. -- n. The language of the Cimbri.
circensial: Of or pertaining to, or held in, the Circus, In Rome. The pleasure of the Circensian shows. Holyday.
circumvest: To cover round, as woth a garment; to invest. (old) Circumvested with much prejudice. Sir H. Wotton.
circumvection: The act of carrying anything around, or the state of being so carried.
circumjovial: One of the moons or satellites of the planet Jupiter. (old) Derham.
citrange: A citrous fruit produced by a cross between the sweet orange and the trifoliate orange (Citrus trifoliata). It is more acid and has a more pronounced aroma than the orange; the tree is hardier. There are several varieties.
citiner: One who is born or bred in a city; a citizen. (old) Champan.
cispadane: On the hither side of the river Po with reference to Rome; that is, on the south side.
cinquecento: The sixteenth century, when applied to Italian art or literature; as, the sculpture of the Cinquecento; Cinquecento style.
ciliform: Having the form of cilia; very fine or slender.
citron: 1. (Bot) A fruit resembling a lemon, but larger, and pleasantly aromatic. The thick rind, when candied, is the citron of commerce. 2. A citron tree. 3. A citron melon. Citron melon. (a) A small variety of muskmelon with sugary greenish flesh. (b) A small variety of watermelon, whose solid white flesh is used in making sweetmeats and preserves.
cinchonism: A condition produced by the excessive or long-continued use of quinine, and marked by deafness, roaring in the ears, vertigo, etc.
circar: A district, or part of a province. See Sircar. [India]
cid: 1. Chief or commander; in Spanish literature, a title of Ruy Diaz, Count of Bivar, a champion of Christianity and of the old Spanish royalty, in the 11th century. 2. An epic poem, which celebrates the exploits of the Spanish national hero, Ruy Diaz.
circumfluous: Flowing round; surrounding in the manner of a fluid. "The deep, circumfluent waves." Pope.
circumfer: To bear or carry round. (old) Bacon.
circumstanced: 1. Placed in a particular position or condition; situated. The proposition is, that two bodies so circumstanced will balance each other. Whewell. 2. Governed by events or circumstances. [Poetic & R.] "I must be circumstanced." Shak.
cicerone: One who shows strangers the curiosities of a place; a guide. Every glib and loquacious hireling who shows strangers about their picture galleries, palaces, and ruins, is termed by them [the Italians] a cicerone, or a Cicero. Trench.
cirriform: Formed like a cirrus or tendril; -- said of appendages of both animals and plants.
cincinnus: A form of monochasium in which the lateral branches arise alternately on opposite sides of the false axis; -- called also scorpioid cyme. --Cin*cin"nal (#), a.
citicism: The manners of a cit or citizen.
circumvention: The act of prevailing over another by arts, address, or fraud; deception; fraud; imposture; delusion. A school in which he learns sly circumvention. Cowper.
cinerescent: Somewhat cinereous; of a color somewhat resembling that of wood ashes.
cisalpine: On the hither side of the Alps with reference to Rome, that is, on the south side of the Alps; -- opposed to transalpine.
circumspectly: In a circumspect manner; cautiously; warily.
circumferential: Pertaining to the circumference; encompassing; encircling; circuitous. Parkhurst.
circumferentially: So as to surround or encircle.
civet: 1. A substance, of the consistence of butter or honey, taken from glands in the anal pouch of the civet (Viverra civetta). It is of clear yellowish or brownish color, of a strong, musky odor,… | To scent or perfume with civet. Cowper
cimbia: A fillet or band placed around the shaft of a column as if to strengthen it. [Written also cimia.]
circumagitate: To agitate on all sides. Jer. Taylor.
cierge: A wax candle used in religous rites.
cippus: A small, low pillar, square or round, commonly having an inscription, used by the ancients for various purposes, as for indicating the distances of places, for a landmark, for sepulchral inscriptions, etc. Gwilt.
circumgestation: The act or process of carrying about. (old) Circumgestation of the eucharist to be adored. Jer. Taylor.
ciclatoun: A costly cloth, of uncertain material, used in the Middle Ages. (old) [Written also checklaton, chekelatoun.] His robe was of ciclatoun, That coste many a Jane. Chaucer.
circean: Having the characteristics of Circe, daughter of Sol and Perseis, a mythological enchantress, who first charmed her victims and then changed them to the forms of beasts; pleasing, but noxious; as, a Circean draught.
circumspectness: Vigilance un guarding against evil from every quarter; caution. [Travel] forces circumspectness on those abroad, who at home are nursed in security. Sir H. Wotton.
cimolite: A soft, earthy, clayey mineral, of whitish or grayish color.
circumincession: The reciprocal existence in each other of the three persons of the Trinity.
cigar: A small roll of tobacco, used for smoking. Cigar fish (Zoöl.), a fish (Decapterus punctatus), allied to the mackerel, found on the coast of the Gulf of Mexico.
cinquefoil: 1. (Bot.) The name of several different species of the genus Potentilla; -- also called five-finger, because of the resemblance of its leaves to the fingers of the hand. 2. (Arch.) An ornamental foliation having five points or cups, used in windows, panels, etc. Gwilt. Marsh cinquefoil, the Potentilla palustris, a plant with purple flowers which grows in fresh-water marshes.
cicatrisive: Tending to promote the formation of a cicatrix; good for healing of a wound.
cistern: 1. An artificial reservoir or tank for holding water, beer, or other liquids. 2. A natural reservoir; a hollow place containing water. "The wide cisterns of the lakes." Blackmore.
circumstance: 1. That which attends, or relates to, or in some way affects, a fact or event; an attendant thing or state of things. The circumstances are well known in the country where they happened. W. Irving. | To place in a particular situation; to suppy relative incidents. The poet took the matters of fact as they came down to him and circumstanced them, after his own manner. Addison.
cite: 1. To call upon officially or authoritatively to appear, as before a court; to summon. The cited dead, Of all past ages, to the general doom Shall hasten. Milton. Cited by finger of God. De Quincey. 2. To urge; to enjoin. Shak. 3. To quote; to repeat, as a passage from a book, or the words of another. The devil can cite Scripture for his purpose. Shak. 4.
circumvolant: Flying around. The circumvolant troubles of humanity. G. Macdonald.
cimbal: A kind of confectionery or cake. (old) Nares.
cimex: A genus of hemipterous insects of which the bedbug is the best known example. See Bedbug.
cidevant: Former; previous; of times gone by; as, a cidevant governor.
cinder: 1. Partly burned or vitrified coal, or other combustible, in which fire is extinct. 2. A hot coal without flame; an ember. Swift. 3. A scale thrown off in forging metal. 4. The slag of a furnace, or scoriaceous lava from a volcano. Cinder frame, a framework of wire in front of the tubes of a locomotive, to arrest the escape of cinders.
circumduct: 1. To lead about; to lead astray. 2. (Law) To contravene; to nullify; as, to circumduct acts of judicature. (old) Ayliffe.
circuiter: One who travels a circuit, as a circuit judge. R. Whitlock.
circumcursation: The act of running about; also, rambling language. (old) Barrow.
circumflect: 1. To bend around. 2. To mark with the circumflex accent, as a vowel.
cilicious: Made, or consisting, of hair. (old) A Cilicious or sackcloth habit. Sir T. Browne.
cimeliarch: A superintendent or keeper of a church's valuables; a churchwarden. (old) Bailey.
circulation: 1. The act of moving in a circle, or in a course which brings the moving body to the place where its motion began. This continual circulation of human things. Swift. 2. The act of passing from place to place or person to person; free diffusion; transmission. The true doctrines of astronomy appear to have had some popular circulation. Whewell. 3. Currency; circulating coin;
circumesophagal: Surrounding the esophagus; -- in Zool. said of the nerve commissures and ganglia of arthropods and mollusks.
cinchonine: One of the quinine group of alkaloids isomeric with and resembling cinchonidine; -- called also cinchonia.
civilizer: One who, or that which, civilizes or tends to civilize.
circumcenter: The center of a circle that circumscribes a triangle.
citole: A musical instrument; a kind of dulcimer. (old)
citified: Aping, or having, the manners of a city.
circus: 1. (Roman Antiq.) A level oblong space surrounded on three sides by seats of wood, earth, or stone, rising in tiers one above another, and divided lengthwise through the middle by a barrier around which the track or course was laid out. It was used for chariot races, games, and public shows. Note: The Circus Maximus at Rome could contain more than 100,000 spectators.
circumrotation: The act of rolling or revolving round, as a wheel; circumvolution; the state of being whirled round. J. Gregory.
circassian: Of or pertaining to Circassia, in Asia. -- n. A native or inhabitant of Circassia.
circumgyrate: To roll or turn round; to cause to perform a rotary or circular motion. Ray.
circumnutate: To pass through the stages of circumnutation.
civilization: 1. The act of civilizing, or the state of being civilized; national culture; refinement. Our manners, our civilization, and all the good things connected with manners, and with civilization, have, in this European world of ours, depended for ages upon two principles -- . . . the spirit of a gentleman, and spirit of religion. Burke 2. (Law) Rendering a criminal process civil.
city: 1. A large town. 2. A corporate town; in the United States, a town or collective body of inhabitants, incorporated and governed by a mayor and aldermen or a city council consisting of a board of… | Of or pertaining to a city. Shak. City council. See under Council. -- City court, The municipal court of a city. [U. S.] -- City ward, a watchman, or the collective watchmen, of a city. (old) Fairfax.
cillosis: A spasmodic trembling of the upper eyelid.
circumnavigate: To sail completely round. Having circumnavigated the whole earth. T. Fuller.
cissoid: A curve invented by Diocles, for the purpose of solving two celebrated problems of the higher geometry; viz., to trisect a plane angle, and to construct two geometrical means between two given straight lines.
citizenship: The state of being a citizen; the status of a citizen.
cilice: A kind of haircloth undergarment. Southey.
circumforanean: Going about or abroad; walking or wandering from house to house. Addison.
cicisbeo: 1. A professed admirer of a married woman; a dangler about women. 2. A knot of silk or ribbon attached to a fan, walking stick, etc. (old)
circle: 1. A plane figure, bounded by a single curve line called its circumference, every part of which is equally distant from a point within it, called the center. 2. citric: Of, pertaining to, or derived from, the citron or lemon; as, citric acid. Citric acid (Chem.), an organic acid, C3H4OH.(CO2H)3, extracted from lemons, currants, gooseberies, etc., as a white crystalline substance, having a pleasant sour taste.
citharistic: Pertaining, or adapted, to the cithara.
cinerary: Pertaining to ashes; containing ashes. Cinerary urns, vessels used by the ancients to preserve the ashes of the dead when burned.
circumcise: 1. To cut off the prepuce of foreskin of, in the case of males, and the internal labia of, in the case of females. 2. (Script.) To purify spiritually.
circumspect: Attentive to all the circustances of a case or the probable consequences of an action; cautious; prudent; wary. Syn. -- See Cautious.
circumpolar: About the pole; -- applied to stars that revolve around the pole without setting; as, circumpolar stars.
cit: A citizen; an inhabitant of a city; a pert townsman; -- used contemptuously. "Insulted as a cit". Johnson Which past endurance sting the tender cit. Emerson.
ciselure: The process of chasing on metals; also, the work thus chased. Weale.
cinchonize: To produce cinchonism in; to poison with quinine or with cinchona.
circumgyratory: Moving in a circle; turning round. Hawthorne.
cincinnatiepoch: An epoch at the close of the American lower Silurian system. The rocks are well developed near Cincinnati, Ohio. The group includes the Hudson River and Lorraine shales of New york.
ciliiform: Having the form of cilia; very fine or slender.
ciliata: One of the orders of Infusoria, characterized by having cilia. In some species the cilia cover the body generally, in others they form a band around the mouth.
circumduction: 1. A leading about; circumlocution. Hooker. 2. An annulling; cancellation. Ayliffe. 3. (Phisiol.) The rotation of a limb round an imaginary axis, so as to describe a concial surface.
circumspection: Attention to all the facts and circumstances of a case; caution; watchfulness. With silent circumspection, unespied. Milton. Syn. -- Caution; prudence; watchfulness; deliberation; thoughtfulness; wariness; forecast.
cingalese: A native or natives of Ceylon descended from its primitive inhabitants; also (sing.), the language of the Cingalese. -- a. Of or pertaining to the Cingalese. [Written also Singhalese.] Note: Ceylonese is applied to the inhabitants of the island in general.
citigradae: A suborder of Arachnoidea, including the European tarantula and the wolf spiders (Lycosidae) and their allies, which capture their prey by rapidly running and jumping. See Wolf spider.
cilia: 1. (Anat.) The eyelashes. 2. (Biol.) Small, generally microscopic, vibrating appendages lining certain organs, as the air passages of the higher animals, and in the lower animals often covering also the whole or a part of the exterior. citigrade: Pertaining to the Citigradæ. -- n. One of the Citigradæ.
cirrobranchiata: A division of Mollusca having slender, cirriform appendages near the mouth; the Scaphopoda.
cinnamene: Styrene (which was formerly called cinnamene because obtained from cinnamic acid). See Styrene.
civily: In a civil manner; as regards civil rights and privileges; politely; courteously; in a well bred manner.
circumstant: Standing or placed around; surrounding. "Circumstant bodies." Sir K. Digby.
circumstantiate: 1. To place in particular circumstances; to invest with particular accidents or adjuncts. If the act were otherwise circumstantiated, it might will that freely which now it wills reluctantly. Bramhall. 2. To prove or confirm by circumstances; to entr into details concerning.
cicada: Any species of the genus Cicada. They are large hemipterous insects, with nearly transparent wings. The male makes a shrill sound by pecular organs in the under side of the abdomen, consisting of a pair of stretched membranes, acted upon by powerful muscles. A noted American species (C. septendecim) is called the seventeen year locust.
cinnamyl: The hypothetical radical, (C6H5.C2H2)2C, of cinnamic compounds. [Formerly written also cinnamule.]
citation: 1. An official summons or notice given to a person to appear; the paper containing such summons or notice. 2. The act of citing a passage from a book, or from another person, in his own words; also, the passage or words quoted; quotation. This horse load of citations and fathers. Milton. 3. Enumeration; mention; as, a citation of facts. 4.
cirrous: 1. (Bot.) Cirrose. 2. (Zoöl.) Tufted; -- said of certain feathers of birds.
circularise: 1. to canvass by distributing letters. Syn. -- circularize. [WordNet 1.5] 2. to distribute circulars to. Syn. -- circularize. [WordNet 1.5] 3. to to pass around, as information. cicatricial: Relating to, or having the character of, a cicatrix. Dunglison.
civilian: 1. One skilled in the civil law. Ancient civilians and writers upon government. Swift. 2. A student of the civil law at a university or college. R. Graves. 3. One whose pursuits are those of civil life, not military or clerical.
civil: 1. Pertaining to a city or state, or to a citizen in his relations to his fellow citizens or to the state; within the city or state. 2. Spenser. 3. Performing the duties of a citizen;
circumscribe: 1. to write or engare around. Thereon is circumscribed this epitaph. Ashmole. 2. To inclose within a certain limit; to hem in; to surround; to bound; to confine; to restrain. Syn. -- To bound; limit; restrict; confine; abridge; restrain;
circlet: 1. A little circle; esp., an ornament for the person, having the form of a circle; that which encircles, as a ring, a bracelet, or a headband. Her fair locks in circlet be enrolled. civic: Relating to, or derived from, a city or citizen; relating to man as a member of society, or to civil affairs. Civic crown (Rom. Antiq.), a crown or garland of oak leaves and acorns, bestowed on a soldier who had saved the life of a citizen in battle.
circumgyration: The act of turning, rolling, or whirling round. A certain turbulent and irregular circumgyration. Holland.
ciliate: Provided with, or surrounded by, cilia; as, a ciliate leaf; endowed with vibratory motion; as, the ciliated epithelium of the windpipe.
circumnavigable: Capable of being sailed round. Ray.
cineritious: Like ashes; having the color of ashes, -- as the cortical substance of the brain.
cinchonaceous: Allied or pertaining to cinchona, or to the plants that produce it.
cilician: Of or pertaining to Cilicia in Asia Minor. -- n. A native or inhabitant of Cilicia.
cinematographer: One who exhibits moving pictures or who takes chronophotographs by the cinematograph. -- Cin`e*mat`o*graph"ic (#), a. -- Cin`e*mat`o*graph"ic*al*ly (#), adv.
cineraria: A Linnæan genus of free-flowering composite plants, mostly from South Africa. Several species are cultivated for ornament.
citizen: 1. One who enjoys the freedom and privileges of a city; a freeman of a city, as distinguished from a foreigner, or one not entitled to its franchises. That large body of the working men who were not… | 1. Having the condition or qualities of a citizen, or of citizens; as, a citizen soldiery. 2. Of or pertaining to the inhabitants of a city; characteristic of citizens; effeminate; luxurious.
circumduce: To declare elapsed, as the time allowed for introducing evidence. Sir W. Scott.
circuline: Proceeding in a circle; circular. (old) "With motion circuline". Dr. H. More.
circumfluence: A flowing round on all sides; an inclosing with a fluid.
circumvolution: 1. The act of rolling round; the state of being rolled. 2. A thing rolled round another. Arbuthnot. 3. A roundabout procedure; a circumlocution. He had neither time nor temper for sentimental circumvolutions. Beaconsfield.
circular: 1. In the form of, or bounded by, a circle; round. 2. repeating itself; ending in itself; reverting to the point of beginning; hence, illogical; inconclusive; as, circular reasoning. 3. | 1. A circular letter, or paper, usually printed, copies of which are addressed or given to various persons; as, a business circular. 2. A sleeveless cloak, cut in circular form.
cion: See Scion. The cion overruleth the stock; and the stock is but passive, and giveth aliment, but no motion, to the graft. Bacon.
cider: The expressed juice of apples. It is used as a beverage, for making vinegar, and for other purposes. Note: Cider was formerly used to signify the juice of other fruits, and other kinds of strong liquor, but was not applied to wine. Cider brandy, a kind of brandy distilled from cider. -- Cider mill, a mill in which cider is made. -- Cider press, the press of a cider mill.
circensian: Of or pertaining to, or held in, the Circus, In Rome. The pleasure of the Circensian shows. Holyday.
circuition: The act of going round; circumlocution.
cingulum: (a) A distinct girdle or band of color; a raised spiral line as seen on certain univalve shells. (b) The clitellus of earthworms. (c) The base of the crown of a tooth.
circumterraneous: Being or dwelling around the earth. "Circumterraneous demouns." H. Hallywell.
circled: Having the form of a circle; round. "Monthly changes in her circled orb." Shak.
cicatrize: To heal or induce the formation of a cicatrix in, as in wounded or ulcerated flesh. Wiseman.
cinctured: Having or wearing a cincture or gridle.
cinque: Five; the number five in dice or cards.
circumclusion: Act of inclosing on all sides.
cinnabar: 1. (Min.) Red sulphide of mercury, occurring in brilliant red crystals, and also in red or brown amorphous masses. It is used in medicine. 2. The artificial red sulphide of mercury used as a pigment; vermilion. Cinnabar Græcorum (. Etym: [L. Graecorum, gen. pl., of the Greeks.] (Med.) Same as Dragon's blood.
circumambient: Surrounding; inclosing or being on all sides; encompassing. "The circumambient heaven." J. Armstrong.
cinura: The group of Thysanura which includes Lepisma and allied forms; the bristletails. See Bristletail, and Lepisma.
cicero: Pica type; -- so called by French printers.
cis: A Latin preposition, sometimes used as a prefix in English words, and signifying on this side.
circumcision: 1. The act of cutting off the prepuce or foreskin of males, or the internal labia of females. Note: The circumcision of males is practiced as a religious rite by the Jews, Mohammedans, etc. 2. (Script.) (a) The Jews, as a circumcised people. (b) Rejection of the sins of the flesh; spiritual purification, and acceptance of the Christian faith.
circumstantiality: The state, characteristic, or quality of being circumstantial; particularity or minuteness of detail. "I will endeavor to describe with sufficient circumstantiality." De Quincey.
cineration: The reducing of anything to ashes by combustion; cinefaction.
cisco: The Lake herring (Coregonus Artedi), valuable food fish of the Great Lakes of North America. The name is also applied to C. Hoyi, a related species of Lake Michigan.
circ: An amphitheatrical circle for sports; a circus. T. Warton.
cicuta: a genus of poisonous umbelliferous plants, of which the water hemlock or cowbane is best known. Note: The name cicuta is sometimes erroneously applied to Conium maculatum, or officinal hemlock.
cicatrix: The pellicle which forms over a wound or breach of continuity and completes the process of healing in the latter, and which subsequently contracts and becomes white, forming the scar.
circination: 1. An orbicular motion. (old) bailey. 2. A circle; a concentric layer. (old) "The circinations and spherical rounds of onions." Sir T. Browne.
circumspective: Looking around everi way; cautious; careful of consequences; watchful of danger. "Circumspective eyes." Pope.
cinematograph: 1. A machine, combining magic lantern and kinetoscope features, for projecting on a screen a series of pictures, moved rapidly (25 to 50 a second) and intermittently before an objective lens, and producing by persistence of vision the illusion of continuous motion; a moving-picture machine; also, any of several other machines or devices producing moving pictorial effects.
cital: 1. Summons to appear, as before a judge. Johnson 2. Citation; quotation Johnson.
circumlocutory: Characterised by circumlocution; periphrastic. Shenstone. The officials set to work in regular circumlocutory order. Chambers's Journal.
cicatrization: The process of forming a cicatrix, or the state of being cicatrized.
cincture: 1. A belt, a girdle, or something worn round the body, -- as by an ecclesiastic for confining the alb. 2. That which encompasses or incloses; an inclosure. "Within the cincture of one wall." Bacon. 3. (Arch.) The fillet, listel, or band next to the apophyge at the extremity of the shaft of a column.
citraconic: Pertaining to, derived from, or having certain characteristics of, citric and aconitic acids. Citraconic acid (Chem.), a white, crystalline, deliquescent substance, C3H4(CO2H)2, obtained by distillation of citric acid. It is a compound of the ethylene series.
ciliary: 1. (Anat.) Pertaining to the cilia, or eyelashes. Also applied to special parts of the eye itself; as, the ciliary processes of the choroid coat; the ciliary muscle, etc. 2. (Biol.) Pertaining to or connected with the cilia in animal or vegetable organisms; as, ciliary motion.
circumscriber: One who, or that which, circumscribes.
citternhead: Blockhead; dunce; -- so called because the handle of a cittern usually ended with a carved head. Marsion
circumnavigation: The act of circumnavigating, or sailing round. Arbuthnot.
circummure: To encompass with a wall. Shak.
cinchonidine: One of the quinine group of alkaloids, found especially in red cinchona bark. It is a white crystalline substance, C19H22N2O, with a bitter taste and qualities similar to, but weaker than, quinine; -- sometimes called also cinchonidia.
cinnamon: (a) The inner bark of the shoots of Cinnamomum Zeylanicum, a tree growing in Ceylon. It is aromatic, of a moderately pungent taste, and is one of the best cordial, carminative, and restorative spices. (b) Cassia. Cinnamon stone (Min.), a variety of garnet, of a cinnamon or hyacinth red color, sometimes used in jewelry.
circumforaneous: Going about or abroad; walking or wandering from house to house. Addison.
cirque: 1. A circle; a circus; a circular erection or arrangement of objects. A dismal cirque Of Druid stones upon a forlorn moor. Keats. 2. A kind of circular valley in the side of a mountain, walled around by precipices of great height.
cirsotomy: Any operation for the removal of varices by incision. Dunglison.
circumstantial: 1. Consisting in, or pertaining to, circumstances or particular incidents. The usual character of human testimony is substantial truth under circumstantial variety. Paley. 2. Incidental; | Something incidental to the main subject, but of less importance; opposed to an essential; -- generally in the plural; as, the circumstantials of religion. Addison.
citadel: A fortress in or near a fortified city, commanding the city and fortifications, and intended as a final point of defense. Syn. - Stronghold. See Fortress.
circumambiency: The act of surrounding or encompassing. Sir T. Browne.
circumvallation: (a) The act of surrounding with a wall or rampart. (b) A line of field works made around a besieged place and the besieging army, to protect the camp of the besiegers against the attack of an enemy from without.
civilize: 1. To reclaim from a savage state; to instruct in the rules and customs of civilization; to educate; to refine. Yet blest that fate which did his arms dispose Her land to civilize, as to subdue. Dryden 2. To admit as suitable to a civilized state. [Obs. or R.] "Civilizing adultery." Milton. Syn. -- To polish; refine; humanize.
circumnutation: The successive bowing or bending in different directions of the growing tip of the stems of many plants, especially seen in climbing plants.
circumference: 1. The line that goes round or encompasses a circular figure; a periphery. Millon. 2. A circle; anything circular. His ponderous shield . . . Behind him cast. The broad circumference Hung on his… | To include in a circular space; to bound. (old) Sir T. Browne.
citatory: Having the power or form of a citation; as, letters citatory.
cirrostomi: The lowest group of vertebrates; -- so called from the cirri around the mouth; the Leptocardia. See Amphioxus.
circumferentor: 1. A surveying instrument, for taking horizontal angles and bearings; a surveyor's compass. It consists of a compass whose needle plays over a circle graduated to 360º, and of a horizontal brass bar at the ends of which are standards with narrow slits for sighting, supported on a tripod by a ball and socket joint. 2. A graduated wheel for measuring tires; a tire circle.
cismontane: On this side of the mountains. See under Ultramontane.
cibation: 1. The act of taking food. 2. (Alchemy) The process or operation of feeding the contents of the crucilbe with fresh material. B. Jonson.
cirrus: 1. (Bot.) A tendril or clasper. 2. (Zoöl.) (a) A soft tactile appendage of the mantle of many Mollusca, and of the parapodia of Annelida. Those near the head of annelids are Tentacular cirri; those of the last segment are caudal cirri. (b) The jointed, leglike organs of Cirripedia. See Annelida, and Polychæta. Note: In some of the inferior animals the cirri aid in locomotion;
circulator: One who, or that which, circulates.
cisted: Inclosed in a cyst. See Cysted.
cirrigerous: Having curled locks of hair; supporting cirri, or hairlike appendages.
circumlocution: The use of many words to express an idea that might be expressed by few; indirect or roundabout language; a periphrese. the plain Billingagate way of calling names . . . would save abundance of time lost by circumlocution. Swift. Circumlocution office, a term of riducle for a governmental office where business is delayed by passing through the hands of different officials.
cima: A kind of molding. See Cyma.
circumscriptly: In a literal, limited, or narrow manner. Milton.
cirsoid: Varicose. Cirsoid aneurism, a disease of an artery in which it becomes dilated and elongated, like a varicose vein.
cinqueports: Five English ports, to which peculiar privileges were anciently accorded; -- viz., Hastings, Romney, Hythe, Dover, and Sandwich; afterwards increased by the addition of Winchelsea, Rye, and some minor places. Baron of the Cinque Ports. See under Baron.
circumstantially: 1. In respect to circumstances; not essentially; accidentally. Of the fancy and intellect, the powers are only circumstantially different. Glanvill. 2. In every circumstance or particular; minutely. To set down somewhat circumstantially, not only the events, but the manner of my trials. Boyle.
circumnavigator: One who sails round. W. Guthrie.
circumvolve: To roll round; to cause to revolve; to put into a circular motion. Herrick.
circumfuse: To pour round; to spread round. His army circumfused on either wing. Milton.
ciceronianism: Imitation of, or resemblance to, the style or action Cicero; a Ciceronian phrase or expression. "Great study in Ciceronianism, the chief abuse of Oxford." Sir P. Sidney.
cinnamone: A yellow crystalline substance, (C6H5.C2H2)2CO, the ketone of cinnamic acid.
cimmerian: 1. Pertaining to the Cimmerii, a fabulous people, said to have lived, in very ancient times, in profound and perpetual darkness. 2. Without any light; intensely dark. In dark Cimmerian desert ever dwell. Milton.
cichoraceous: Belonging to, or resembling, a suborder of composite plants of which the chicory (Cichorium) is the type.
cindery: Resembling, or composed of, cinders; full of cinders.
cibol: A perennial alliaceous plant (Allium fistulosum), sometimes called Welsh onion. Its fistular leaves areused in cookery.
cistercian: A monk of the prolific branch of the Benedictine Order, established in 1098 at Cîteaux, in France, by Robert, abbot of Molesme. For two hundred years the Cistercians followed the rule of St. Benedict in all its rigor. -- a. Of or pertaining to the Cistercians.
citrine: Like a citron or lemon; of a lemon color; greenish yellow. Citrine ointment (Med.), a yellowish mercurial ointment, the unquentum hydrargyri nitratis. | A yellow, pellucid variety of quartz.
circumjacence: Condition of being circumjacent, or of bordering ou every side.
cirsocele: The varicose dilatation of the spermatic vein.
cinnamic: Pertaining to, or obtained from, cinnamon. Cinnamic acid (Chem.), a white, crystalline, odorless substance. C6H5.C2H2C2H2.CO2H, formerly obtained from storax and oil of cinnamon, now made from certain benzene derivatives in large quantities, and used for the artificial production of indigo.
